would_have_shipped_defects.summary: No reproduction was performed and the fix was never executed once: the report's 'How verified' rests entirely on shellcheck plus a man-page reading of `-a`, so the DoD's before/after reproduction evidence is absent.
would_have_shipped_defects.why_blocking: The order makes 'Reproduce first' scope item 1 and a merge condition ('reproduction evidence in the report (before: the collision + stranded state; after: clean allocation + recovery print)'), precisely because a plausible form-based fix had already been observed to fail in practice on this exact bug — the order records that `new-window -t hive -n <task>` with no index 'fails identically', so reasoning from the manual about tmux target resolution had already produced one wrong answer. The attempt's sole justification for `-a` is that same class of reasoning. The 40-line `print_half_launch_recovery` path has likewise never been run, so its first execution would be at the moment an operator is mid-recovery. The reviewer holding the DoD bounces this; an isolated replay was available without the excluded blast radius (a private `tmux -L` socket needs no spine emits and never touches the operator's live server), so the order's named-risk escape hatch ('if the drill can't simulate an occupied index portably') does not cover the gap.
